title: Adaptive Compliance Tiering Controller for Audit Logs (tenant-aware RBAC & SSO mapping)
creator: Marin Alvarez
description: Design and implement an Adaptive Compliance Tiering Controller for the audit ingestion pipeline and storage subsystem. The controller enforces per-tenant and per-actor retention rules derived from RBAC v2 roles and SSO/SAML attribute mappings, applies cost-aware tiering decisions (hot/hot-warm/cold) and automatic shard compaction, and emits audit-quality signals for downstream compliance verification.
acceptance_criteria: Controller applies retention tiers based on tenant regulatory tags and RBAC role-derived retention policies
SSO/SAML attribute enrichment is persisted on audit events and used in index partition keys for fast querying
Automatic coldspill to object store for cold-tier events reduces hotstore ingestion cost by >=20% on representative workload
HMAC chain integrity header present on all rolled-up shards and verifiable by compliance service
Metrics and dashboard exist showing tiering decisions, cost savings, and per-tenant retention adherence
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope: controller API, policy engine, enrichment hook, coldspill mechanism. Action: prototype policy DSL.

2025-02-19: PoC DSL implemented. RBAC v2 mapping table sketch reviewed with Auth team; needs canonical attribute names from SAML team (nameid, eduPersonAffiliation) — blocking until ENG-75411 provides mapping.

2025-02-26: Chose hybrid strategy: time-based + event-type override (e.g., admin-login events default to longer retention). Decided HMAC chain approach for shard integrity with compact proof metadata stored separately.

2025-03-01: Prototype tested on replay of 48h audit traffic (tenant mix). Coldspill reduced hotstore QPS by 28% and storage bill estimate down 22%. Found edge case: pre-indexed events missing SSO attributes — added fallback enrichment via session-lookup service.
2025-03-04: Security review requested. Planning canary rollout on non-prod tenants with gradual ramp over 2 weeks. Next: finalize indexing keys and implement canary rollback hooks.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit + integration tests, run synthesis on synthetic workloads
Stage 1: Canary on internal org (10% of internal events) with alerting for retention mismatch
Stage 2: Canary on non-prod tenant cohort (5 tenants) with telemetry validation
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% production traffic, validate cost and SLOs
Stage 4: Full rollout with runtime-1.22 release and post-mortem review
